sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises steeply as the share of the credit limit in use climbs, with the largest increases above roughly 0.6.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk rises with it, mainly going from zero to one or two delinquencies.
The two drivers reinforce each other: the effect of utilization is much larger for applicants with two delinquencies than for applicants with none.
Income has a moderate effect, with risk falling as income rises.
Length of credit history has a moderate effect, with risk falling as the history gets longer.
Debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, with risk somewhat higher above about 0.44.
Age hardly matters, and the data do not settle whether the number of dependents or months at the current address matter at all.
The data do not settle whether recent credit inquiries have a negligible effect, since their contribution is small and its band is wide.
